decisions.evidence: The current valuation proof avoids Dedekind--Kummer's global monogeneity hypothesis and agrees with Milne Proposition 3.53.
The buffered count N(T+2)-N(T-1) covers both closed endpoints and the compact initial range is handled separately.
The repaired local DVR residue layers and free-rank calculation prove the residue-degree identity without the former chain assertion.
The reader's DVR-layer and CRT proof is mathematically sound; Alpha additionally completed the required high-risk review of quotient cardinalities and unit-ideal boundary.
The repaired finite quotient, local DVR exponent, localization, and CRT argument is choice-free; Alpha added the required high-risk disposition.
The Mellin continuation and its residue at zero now license every evaluated value and sign; Alpha added the required contour and boundary risk disposition.
At s=1 the former hypotheses held while zeta'/zeta has a pole and the displayed right side is finite; the statement and Given clause now explicitly exclude s=1.
The rank-one computation is unchanged and its source now points to the applicable Etingof exercise instead of the unrelated live document.
The source repair is applicable and the current no-positive-integral-pairing argument proves simplicity; Alpha added the required high-risk linkage review.
The explicit sl2 singular powers and embedding directions agree with the dot-action convention, and the corrected Etingof source is exact.
The current vector-partition comparison includes the rank-one boundary and supplies the formerly vague growth argument.
The sl2 commutator and PBW nonvanishing establish the singular vector with exponent n+1; Alpha added the required high-risk review and checked the corrected source.
The current PBW-model kernel argument through gr U(n-minus)=S(n-minus) licenses injectivity.
Both implications now retain positive-integral linkage and expose PBW injectivity; Alpha completed the required biconditional risk review.
The Jantzen-derived reflection now has its required positive-integral pairing, and Alpha reviewed both directions against Etingof Theorem 20.13 and Corollary 20.14.
The proof now invokes the exact arbitrary-root result rather than a false simple-root reduction; Alpha completed the required high-risk source and boundary review.
Regular dominance alone allows irrational coroot pairings and no linkage edge; the counterexample witness now explicitly uses a regular dominant integral A2 weight.
The Bruhat embedding poset fails for regular nonintegral weights; the title, Example, verification, manifest, and contract now require regular integral dominance.
The current corollary restricts to the irreducible character-field model, where the scalar multiplicity is the Schur index and the dimension formula gives divisibility.
The definition now chooses a finite cyclotomic Galois splitting field, exactly matching the decomposition theorem it invokes.
The current example correctly separates the rational Galois-orbit multiplicity from Schur index one over Q(zeta).

Alpha replaced the refuter-confirmed miscitation route with the irreducible rational Hamilton-quaternion module and direct complex-character computation 2 chi; its contract and prior high-risk record are synchronized.
The repaired field tower licenses character determination, and Alpha's required high-risk review checks both stabilizer implications and the fixed-field conclusion.
Characteristic zero and finite dimensionality now license complete reducibility, and the semilinear Galois action preserves multiplicities.
The finite-Galois hypotheses and common-overfield comparison are sound; Alpha added the required multiplicity-preservation risk review.
The theorem now uses the relative scalar-extension multiplicity for arbitrary F, and Alpha reviewed the orbit character and dimension formulas under that convention.
Alpha supplied an explicit trace-dual-basis descent proof for the Galois-stable isotypic sum, removed its unused dependency, synchronized manifest/contract data, and completed the high-risk review.
The reader's scalar-multiplicity proof replaces the false Morita claim, and Alpha's critical-risk review checks attainability, divisibility, minimality, and the iff case.
The reader's character-field restriction and centrality proof are sound; Alpha also fixed operatorname and 1 tensor z, regenerated the contract, and completed the high-risk review.
The cited endomorphism base-change lemma did not imply descent; current step 2.1 proves X=E tensor X^Gamma with trace-dual bases and then uses irreducibility.
The former cited theorem did not prove m_Q(chi) divides chi(1); the repaired Hamilton-quaternion construction directly exhibits the irreducible rational module with complex character 2 chi.
Fact L4's missing backslash made the endomorphism expression malformed; it is now the well-formed command operatorname{End}.
For z in D_V the tensor z tensor 1 was ill-typed in E tensor_K D_V; the proof now uses the invariant element 1 tensor z.
